title.narrative: Life-Saving Nutrition Interventions for Children and Pregnant and Lactating Women in Afgoye District of Lower shabele region- Somalia

description.narrative: ltpgtSomalia is facing a severe humanitarian crisis driven by prolonged drought, consecutive poor rainy seasons, and major funding shortfalls. The post-Gu 2025 FSNAU analysis and recent PAC assessment confirm that, despite localized rainfall in parts of southern Somalia, overall precipitation remained below average, resulting in water scarcity, reduced agricultural production, declining river levels, and weakened livestock productivity. These shocks have severely eroded household coping capacity, particularly among children under five, pregnant and lactating women, and poor agropastoral households.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtAs a result, acute food insecurity is projected to rise from 3.4 million people in September to 4.4 million between October and December 2025. The cumulative effects of a severely dry Xagaa season, forecasted poor Deyr rains, and the approaching Jilaal dry season are expected to further worsen conditions, increasing the risk of IPC Phase 4 (Emergency) and localized IPC Phase 5 (Famine) outcomes. Vulnerability is escalating rapidly in riverine and agropastoral areas, urban IDP settlements, and pastoral zones.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe drought has intensified water shortages as traditional water sources dry up or become contaminated, and boreholes become non-functional due to overuse and poor maintenance. Reliance on costly water trucking has increased, alongside disease outbreaks and livestock losses. Women and girls face disproportionate burdens and protection risks while accessing water.ltbrgtSimultaneously, funding cuts have forced the closure or scale-down of essential health and nutrition services, disrupting access to therapeutic feeding, micronutrient supplementation, and maternal health care. An estimated 1.85 million children under five are projected to suffer from acute malnutrition in the coming year, with preventive nutrition supplies for children and pregnant and lactating women expected to be depleted by the end of November. These disruptions are likely to increase malnutrition caseloads and mortality, particularly in areas with critical GAM rates (gt15%).lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtIn Afgoye District, Lower Shabelle, food security and nutrition outcomes continue to deteriorate due to reduced Shabelle River flow, poor off-season harvests, high population density, and the presence of vulnerable host communities and IDPs. Market dependence combined with declining purchasing power has further limited access to adequate food and nutrition, while reduced maternal and child health services have heightened risks of preventable illness and death.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtltbgtPhysicians Across Continents has provided integrated health and nutrition services in Afgoye District since 2019 with UNICEF support however, nutrition activities have been fully suspended following funding cuts, leaving a critical service gap that has directly affected more than 500 children with severe acute malnutrition and 26,246 pregnant and lactating womenlt/bgt.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe proposed project will address ltbgtthis gap by delivering integrated, life-saving nutrition services for children under five and pregnant and lactating women in Afgoye District through supporting 1 fixed OTPs, 2 mobile teams, and 1 SC in Dolawe Centerlt/bgt. The intervention will include: nutrition screening and referral treatment of severe acute malnutrition through supported stabilization care management of moderate acute malnutrition through TSFP, improved home diets (Kobciye Shurbad), micronutrient supplementation, and IYCF counselling community-based SBCC interventions training of health workers and community nutrition workers on IMAM and MIYCN routine MUAC screening at facility and community levels and piloting Family MUAC with 300 caregivers to strengthen early identification and referral.ltbrgtBy restoring access to essential nutrition services and strengthening prevention and early detection, the project will reduce excess morbidity and mortality and help avert further deterioration of nutrition outcomes in Afgoye District.ltbrgtlt/pgt
